claims.text: P19 holds over 300 seeded random statements (v1 and v2, cash about the £2,500 limit on both sides, ambiguous, unexplained, withdrawal, gambling lines) and all nine synthetic archetype/profile cases: M18's evidence is exactly the credits categorised cash_deposit, each is in M2's evidence, M18 <= M2, and every cash deposit at or above the single-deposit limit is in the judgement queue carrying the single_cash_deposit indicator's id; also at a firm limit of £100.01; and the queue holds every unexplained credit and every indicator-flagged line exactly once, largest amount first, statement order between ties.

Contract tests: an ambiguous credit is queued with each candidate (from its conflict form) and the category and bucket it would give (payment-method cue: none); profile:director / profile:own_account give their kind's bucket; possible own-account transfers are queued only when given, each with the lines it could pair with; the function leaves the statement unchanged and is deterministic; `cma run` writes judgement_queue into its evidence record.
Full suite, lint and compile pass.
claims.proof_cmd: ruff check src tests && python -m compileall -q src && python -m pytest -q
python -m pytest -q -m "invariants or contracts or dual_run"

claims.proof_output: 9/9 memos fully grounded; model = fake; ruleset = v1

notes: Committed as 5973c5a on bridgie-task/statement-review/T09. indicators.judgement_queue(statement, indicators, possible_own_account=None) is a pure function in the figures layer (design C2): unexplained credits (category other; ambiguous when the rule id is a conflict form, with queue_candidates giving each candidate's category from that ruleset's table, or the profile kind's category, and the CREDIT_BUCKET bucket), every line of each possible own-account group when the caller supplies them (R8/R9 pairing is Tier 2 and not built, so cma run passes none), and every indicator's evidence lines. One entry per line, ordered by absolute pence descending then statement order; no money arithmetic. New models QueueEntry and QueueCandidate (additive). The production caller is graph._indicator_fields, so cma run's evidence record gains an additive judgement_queue key (R53); the checkpoint allow-list is unchanged since the queue is computed at evidence time from stored lines. The workspace display (R15's case view) is T21's. A queue entry's amount is the line's signed float as the statement gives it; ordering uses pence.
